summary: The five CL-6 proposals are consistent with each other, and each is needed, but only with four amendments that wave 1 does not state. I built a lattice-level model on the real substrate (net-cell-write auto-tagging, promote-cell-to-tagged, BSP and the drain). With all of them in place — the ev_W read (a), a flat per-key ⊤ (row 2), unify-fire writing both sides (e), no network-wide viewpoint (b), and lifting with labelled outputs (c) — it gives DFS's answers on 8/8 rows under 3 schedules. Dropping any one part breaks at least one row (rows still right: 5/8, 2/8, 7/8, 6/8, 6/8). DEFERRED 177's filed fix ((a)+row 2+(e)) fixes its own three rows but not two more wrong-answer shapes I found on the shipped solver: `(pick ?x) (pick ?y) (= ?x ?y)` LOSES {x 2, y 2}, and `(pick ?x) (= ?x 2)` returns {x 1} {x 2} {x 1}. Both also need (b) and (c). (b) as written (delete cell-1 as the fallback viewpoint) would break elaboration's commit-by-keeping-the-bit (meta-universe.rkt:257-263; test-speculation-bridge.rkt:69-88). It would also send speculative networks into the Tier-1 flush (DEFERRED 178). The repair: a grow-only premise set P, read as W_p ∪ P; cell-1 retired as the tag source; Tier-1 dispatch on α. C8-5's anti-monotone guard mask comes from encoding nogoods as worldview bits. With nogood environments the same decision kills 0/144 passing rows, against 24/144 with bits. So (d) becomes: live and answers are read only over completed nogoods. D.2's two-phase set survives only as the codomain of the derived projection α = (C, X), which is monotone over 1 115 steps and whose live read equals today's cell-1. It does not survive as a cell with writers. Of cell-1's 11 production writers, one (make-branch-pu) is dead. test-tagged-cell-value.rkt:210-224 must flip. test-solver-context.rkt:341-362 need not: it is the regression catcher, failing under D.2's literal row 1 and passing once the viewpoint is per query. The existing DFS↔ATMS parity suite has no conflicting-binding case. A scratch extension with these rows fails 5/7 at HEAD in 0.2 s, and is the test layer to land with the fix.

verdicts.question: Q1 (overall): are proposals (a)–(f) consistent with each other?
verdicts.amendment: They are consistent, and each part is needed. Four amendments: (A1) (b) must not simply delete the fallback viewpoint. An unlabelled S0 fire reads at W_p ∪ P, where P is a grow-only set of committed premises, because elaboration commits a speculation by keeping its bit (elab-speculation-bridge.rkt:305-309). Only live = C ∧ ¬X is banned inside S0. (A2) (b) must also retire cell-1 as the TAG source in net-cell-write (propagator.rkt:2011-2017) and net-cell-write-widen (:4065-4069). Otherwise an unconditional write made after any assumption is labelled with all of them, which is the R6 mechanism. BSP's Tier-1 dispatch (:3410, `(zero? worldview)`) must read 'assumptions exist' from α. (A3) '⊤ ⇒ nogood' is a property of the READ, not of a stored entry. In 177's row 2 the base is {x a} and the entry is {x b}; no entry is ⊤, but ev_W is. The rule is: ev_W has a ⊤ component ⇒ nogood(W), detected at the boundary read or by a lifted check fire. (A4) (c) is one rule. Each output entry is labelled with the W its inputs were read at (soundness). The fire is evaluated at every W a boundary will query, or once per input label when it is additive (completeness). Evidence that each part is needed (model rows that go wrong when it is dropped): (a): R2, R6, R7. Row 2: 6 rows, and R5 becomes schedule-dependent. (e): R3. (b): R6, R7. (c): R5, R8.
verdicts.evidence: MEASUREMENT. `racket w26-combined.rkt` (scratch; real propagator.rkt + decision-cell.rkt). Rows matching DFS under BSP, drain and drain with reversed install, out of 8: TODAY 1. (a) only 1. (a)+row2 3. (a)+row2+(e) [= DEFERRED 177's fix shape] 4. +(b) with static labels 6. FULL (a)+row2+(e)+(b)+(c) 8. FULL minus (e) 7. FULL minus (a) 5. FULL minus row2 2 (and R5 schedule-dependent). FULL keeping cell-1 as viewpoint and tag source 6. FULL with per-entry lifting 8. Per-entry lifting with today's unify 7. Rows: R1 `two`, R2 `q3`, R3 `clash`, R4 `agree` (DEFERRED 177's table); R5 cross-site unify, R6 base write after the branch, R7 (production-verified in w26-crosssite.out); R8 (model only).
verdicts.power_check: The model's TODAY configuration reproduces production's ATMS answers exactly on R1 {x b}, R2 {b}{a}, R3, R4 and R6 (the triple {a}{b}{a}), and on R7 under BSP. It does not reproduce R5's exact production answer (model: 4 answers; production: 1). Both are wrong against DFS; production's arg↔param links are not modelled. The schedule-independence check fired where it should: TODAY R7 and R8, and FULL minus row2 R5. Every single-part ablation loses at least one row, so the method can fail.

verdicts.question: Q1(a): the read is ev_W = base ⊔ matching entries (C4-1, C9-3)
verdicts.amendment: (i) The law needs a JOIN domain merge. On LWW, (a) alone fixes nothing (1/8), and R2 stays wrong ({x b}), so (a) ships with row 2, and with row 8 for type cells. (ii) The compat path (decision-cell.rkt:472, 'first match' when no domain merge is given) has 3 production callers: meta-universe.rkt:280, metavar-store.rkt:504 and propagator.rkt:4511. They must pass the cell's merge, and the compat path is deleted. (iii) ⊤ is detected at reads (A3), so C9-5's wording 'a ⊤ component in a tagged entry' must say 'in ev_W'.
verdicts.evidence: w26-combined.out: FULL minus (a) gets R2, R6, R7 wrong (5/8). w26-label-soundness.out: closure evaluation with the production reader is incomplete on 91/3200 checks for a non-additive f; with ev_W, 0/3200. PRECEDENT inside the codebase: typing-propagators.rkt:655-731 already hand-rolls ev_W for the attribute map (`tagged-attribute-map-read-with-base-merge`, whose comment names exactly this defect), staged with zero consumers.
verdicts.power_check: The production-reader row is flagged (91/3200), and dropping (a) from FULL loses 3 rows.

verdicts.question: Q1(b): cell-1 split — information as α(decisions, nogoods), viewpoint W per propagator or per query (C4-4, C2-4)
verdicts.amendment: Amendments A1 and A2. Cell-1 has THREE roles today, not two: (1) information, (2) a per-query viewpoint, and (3) the default viewpoint of every unlabelled reader, which is how a committed speculation stays visible. Role 3 becomes the premise set P: grow-only, written at commit, read as W_p ∪ P. Reading P is monotone because ev is monotone in W for join domains. The viewpoint-per-query part holds exactly as C4-4 proposed.
verdicts.evidence: w26-viewpoint.out Part 1 (the test-solver-context.rkt:341-362 sequence): A, production replacement merge: (val-left val-right). B, merge = ior (D.2 row 1): (val-right) [C4-4 reproduced]. C/D/E, W passed per query, never written to cell-1: (val-left val-right) under the ior merge, the replacement merge, and the ev_W read. w26-premise.out (committed h1, failed h2; reads along one command): TODAY (bot Bool Bool top Bool), 1 non-monotone step. (b) with no commit rule: bot throughout, which fails test-speculation-bridge.rkt:69-88. (b) reading live inside S0: same as TODAY, non-monotone. (b)+P: (bot bot Bool Bool Bool), monotone, final Bool. w26-combined.out: FULL keeping cell-1 as viewpoint and tag source gets R6 and R7 wrong (6/8). T1: under (b) a speculative network has cell-1 = 0, takes the Tier-1 flush, and the dependent unify fires 0 times (wrong answer). The control with a plain propagator fires it 2 times (right answer).
verdicts.power_check: Leg B reproduces C4-4's lost answer. The B-BARE leg shows the regression the meta-universe.rkt:257-263 comment records. T1's plain-propagator control and the drain both give DFS's answer.

verdicts.question: Q1(c): labelled fires write only tagged cells, promotion at the topology tier (C9-4); lifting additive or on the union-closure (C4-7)
verdicts.amendment: State it as A4. Two consequences: (i) Closure evaluation is exponential in independent branch sites. On R5 it took 341 unify evaluations against 29 for per-entry lifting, so declaring a fire additive matters, and (e) makes unify additive. (ii) Each promotion builds a fresh tagged-merge closure (propagator.rkt:1815). Closing labelledness downstream therefore multiplies the per-closure merge identities that CL-4(b) shows fence fail-closed. The fence must be keyed on the combinator term (`join:tagged d`), not on the closure.
verdicts.evidence: THEOREM. Hypotheses: D is a join-semilattice; ev_W(t) = base ⊔ ⨆{v | b ⊆ W}; f is monotone; every output entry is (W, f(ev_W(in))). Then ev_V(out) ⊑ f(ev_V(in)) for every V, and equality holds when V is an evaluation point, or when f is additive and every input label is one. Checked by enumeration in w26-label-soundness.out (400 inputs × 8 viewpoints = 3 200 checks per row): closure-evaluated: unsound 0, incomplete 0, for additive and non-additive f. Per input label: unsound 0; incomplete 0 for additive f and 4 for non-additive. Power rows: plain output read at a viewpoint (C9-4's static-plain shape) unsound 393 and 188; under-labelled output unsound 63 and 31. w26-combined.out: (a)+row2+(e)+(b) with static labels gets R5 and R8 wrong, and FULL with closure or per-entry lifting gets them right.
verdicts.power_check: Both power rows are flagged, and removing (c) loses R5 (a production-verified lost answer) and R8.

verdicts.question: Q1(d): invalidation only at boundaries, over completed inputs (C8-5)
verdicts.amendment: C8-5's anti-monotonicity lives in the ENCODING, not in the decision. Under (b) a guard or NAF writes a nogood environment ({G} ∪ the label of the row it read) to the existing nogood cell (atms.rkt:229-231; solver-state-consistent?). That write is monotone in the materialized rows. So: S0 may write nogoods from upward-closed tests (⊤ under W; a guard failing on a ground input). The non-monotone step is reading live or answers, which must wait for completed nogoods (BC-4). NAF stays at S1, because its inner goal's fixpoint is needed. Today the guard AND-NOTs cell-1 from inside S0 (relations.rkt:2331-2349), while process-fork-contradiction and NAF are already boundary handlers (typing-propagators.rkt:1515-1521; relations.rkt:357).
verdicts.evidence: w26-guard-nogood.out, exhaustive: 3 rows sharing G, 8 pass/fail patterns, 6 arrival orders, the guard deciding after every arrival. The bit mask AND-NOTed into a grow-only set kills 24/144 passing rows. Nogood environments kill 0/144. C8's own case: pass row alive #f with bits, #t with environments.
verdicts.power_check: Failing rows left alive: 0/144 under both encodings, so the environment encoding is not trivially permissive. The bit encoding reproduces C8-5.

verdicts.question: Q1(e): unify-fire writes each side into the other (C4-12)
verdicts.amendment: Also needed for lifting: (v1, v2) ↦ (v2, v1) is a join-homomorphism, so per-entry lifting is exact for unify. Today's fire, which writes nothing when both sides are bound and differ (relations.rkt:2112-2120), is not monotone.
verdicts.evidence: w26-combined.out: FULL minus (e) gets R3 `clash` wrong (7/8). Per-entry lifting with (e): 8/8. Per-entry lifting with today's unify: R3 wrong.
verdicts.power_check: The ablation loses exactly the row the mechanism predicts (DEFERRED 177's row 3).

verdicts.question: Q1(f): is D.2's two-phase set still needed once (b) is in place?
verdicts.amendment: It is needed only as the CODOMAIN of the derived projection α = (C, X), where C is the bits of every assumption made and X = C ∧ ¬decisions-bitmask. It has one writer, the projection, and its ior is a property of α, not of 10 writers. X cannot carry the multi-assumption nogoods that guards and NAF produce, so the nogood cell sits beside it, and P (A1) is added. Restate D.2 row 1 and BC-2: cell-1 := α(assumptions, decisions, nogoods), with live derived only at boundaries.
verdicts.evidence: w26-viewpoint.out Part 2, on the real decisions-state: over the test-solver-context.rkt:117-140 sequence plus 500 random sequences (1 115 steps), today's projection is non-monotone on 215 steps (1 on the test's own sequence), α is non-monotone on 0, and live(α) ≠ today's cell-1 on 0.
verdicts.power_check: The method flags the projection's narrowing steps (215).

verdicts.question: Q2: cell-1's production writers at HEAD (C2-4's inventory), and what each becomes
verdicts.amendment: All 11 sites are confirmed, and one is dead. Writer → what it becomes: 1. atms.rkt:281, solver-assume's eager recompute: deleted. Tags come from the writer, and α covers 'exists'. 2. atms.rkt:595, solver-state-with-worldview (viewpoint): W carried per query. 3. propagator.rkt:978-987, the projection, installed at atms.rkt:237: becomes α's single writer. 4. propagator.rkt:2412, make-branch-pu: DEAD; its only callers are in tests/test-branch-pu.rkt. Delete it, or pass W. 5. elab-speculation-bridge.rkt:290, ior of the hyp bit: the thunk already gets W (:296-300); on success write P := P ∪ {h}. 6. elab-speculation-bridge.rkt:326, AND-NOT on failure: a nogood {h} ∪ ctx (already recorded) and no cell-1 write. The snapshot restore at :318 remains a non-monotone boundary act (C9-4). 7. typing-propagators.rkt:1192-1194, the fork-on-union handler (ior N bits): branch aids enter α through the decisions and assumptions cells. 8. typing-propagators.rkt:1501-1506, process-fork-contradiction (AND-NOT): nogood {aid} per contradicted branch, at the boundary. 9. relations.rkt:238-240, NAF per-binding mask: nogood {naf} ∪ row label, at S1. 10. relations.rkt:351-353, NAF single bit: nogood {naf} ∪ outer label, at S1. 11. relations.rkt:2346-2349, the guard fire in S0: nogood {g} ∪ the label it read (monotone). Readers that must move as well: net-cell-read :1601-1606 and resolve-worldview-bitmask/pnet :4479-4486 → W_p ∪ P. net-cell-write :2011-2017 and net-cell-write-widen :4065-4069 → tag only from the writer's W. The Tier-1 dispatch :3410 → α. meta-universe.rkt:288-300 → W_p ∪ P. metavar-store.rkt:504, which already ignores cell-1 and so disagrees with meta-universe.rkt today → W_p ∪ P. relations.rkt:2418-2419, which finds the guard's bit by XOR of cell-1 → use the returned aid. relations.rkt:2874 and :2959, dissolution → a boundary read of live(α). typing-propagators.rkt:700-703 → unused helper.
verdicts.evidence: `grep -n 'worldview-cache-cell-id' racket/prologos/*.rkt` with comment lines dropped: 11 write sites (the 10 listed by C4-4 plus the projection), and `(cell-id 1)` has no alias besides propagator.rkt:623. `grep -rn make-branch-pu --include=*.rkt racket/prologos` with tests and benchmarks excluded: only the export (:140) and the definition (:2406).
verdicts.power_check: The same grep finds every site that C2-4 and C4-4 listed independently. The dead-code grep finds make-branch-pu's 5 call sites in tests/test-branch-pu.rkt when tests are included.

verdicts.question: Q3: which tests pin today's semantics and must flip, which catch a regression; lattice probes on the combined design
verdicts.amendment: The triage's claim holds for test-tagged-cell-value.rkt:210-224 and FAILS for test-solver-context.rkt:341-362, whose assertions hold under the combined design. MUST FLIP. (1) test-tagged-cell-value.rkt:210-217 and :219-224 pin cell-1's replacement merge. (2) test-tagged-cell-value.rkt:244-251, :264-279, :295-320 and :324-340 take the viewpoint or tag from cell-1 (b). The content survives with W from the writer or reader. (3) test-tagged-cell-value.rkt:51-54, :61-66, :68-79, :81-94 and :526-537 pin 'entry shadows base', 'most specific wins' and the compat first-match read on symbol values that have no join (a). Retarget them to a join domain, or delete them with the compat path. (4) test-solver-context.rkt:96-115, :117-140 and :163-180 read raw cell-1; the content is preserved as live(α) (0 mismatches). (5) test-solver-context.rkt:309-316 pins the eager write at atms.rkt:281. (6) test-solver-context.rkt:326-339 pins 'a write after assume is tagged by cell-1', which is the R6 defect channel. (7) test-union-types-atms.rkt:148-210 and :418-455 pin AND-NOT and ior on cell-1. The E2E tests at :596-670 keep their content (1/0/2 surviving bits) as live(α). (8) test-branch-pu.rkt:58-63 tests make-branch-pu, which is dead. (9) test-specialized-cells.rkt:263-325 tests warm-cache plumbing; change the form or retire it. CATCH A REGRESSION. test-solver-context.rkt:341-362 fails under D.2's literal row 1. test-speculation-bridge.rkt:69-88 fails if (b) lands without P. test-tagged-cell-value.rkt:371-429 (isolation) stays valid, but uses a replace domain, so it cannot see (a). test-solver-parity.rkt has 15 cases and none with a conflicting binding, so it is blind to DEFERRED 177 until extended.
verdicts.evidence: `raco test` at HEAD, one file per process (w26-baseline-tests.out): test-tagged-cell-value 51 passed, test-solver-context 30, test-speculation-bridge 27, test-union-types-atms 27, test-solver-parity 15. So every 'must flip' line is an assertion that passes today. Lattice probes on the combined design: w26-combined, w26-viewpoint, w26-premise, w26-label-soundness and w26-guard-nogood (verdicts above).
verdicts.power_check: Leg B of w26-viewpoint reproduces the failure of :341-362 under ior. w26-premise's B-BARE leg reproduces the :69-88 failure. w26-parity-ext shows that the parity harness, once extended, fails 5/7 at HEAD.

verdicts.question: Q4: at the lattice level, does the combined proposal fix DEFERRED 177's three rows?
verdicts.amendment: Yes: all three rows and the control, under BSP, the drain and the drain with reversed install. Amendment: 177's filed fix shape ((a) read, (b) unify both sides, (c) flat ⊤) is not enough for the same defect class. On the production-verified R5 (a lost answer) and R6 (the row-2 class with the binding after the branch) it stays wrong in the model until the viewpoint is per-propagator (b) and fires are lifted (c). Add R5 and R6 to 177's table, and give the fix shape the (b)+(c) parts with A1–A3.
verdicts.evidence: w26-combined.out: FULL 8/8; (a)+row2+(e) [177's fix] 4/8, with R1–R4 right and R5–R8 wrong. Production, w26-crosssite.out via tools/scratch-run.sh: R5 `(rel [?x ?y] (pick ?x) (pick ?y) (= ?x ?y))`: ATMS @[{:x 1, :y 1}], DFS @[{:x 1, :y 1} {:x 2, :y 2}]. R6 `(rel [?x] (pick ?x) (= ?x 2))`: ATMS @[{:x 1} {:x 2} {:x 1}], DFS @[{:x 2}]. R7: both @[{:x 1, :y 1}]. w26-parity-ext.out, the same shapes through the Racket parity harness: 177 rows 1–3 FAIL, R5 FAIL, R6 FAIL, agree and R7 PASS, 3/3 copied controls PASS.
verdicts.power_check: The model's TODAY configuration gets 1/8 rows right and reproduces production's wrong answers on R1–R3 and R6. Each ablation of FULL loses at least one 177 row or new row.

findings.claim_attacked: DEFERRED 177: 'All three parts are needed; each covers a different row', with the fix shape (a) read base ⊔ matching, (b) unify both sides, (c) flat ⊤.
findings.evidence: Two more wrong-answer shapes on the shipped solver at HEAD (w26-crosssite.prologos, tools/scratch-run.sh; replicated through the Racket parity harness in w26-parity-ext.out). (1) `(pick ?x) (pick ?y) (= ?x ?y)`: ATMS @[{:x 1, :y 1}] against DFS @[{:x 1, :y 1} {:x 2, :y 2}]. An answer is LOST; every 177 row so far added answers. (2) `(pick ?x) (= ?x 2)`: ATMS @[{:x 1} {:x 2} {:x 1}] against DFS @[{:x 2}]. Mechanism of (2), reproduced exactly by the model's TODAY configuration: after pick promotes the scope cell and solver-assume writes every bit into cell-1 (atms.rkt:281), the bitmask-0 write x = 2 is labelled with cell-1 by net-cell-write's fallback (propagator.rkt:2011-2017). The binding meant to be unconditional becomes conditional on all the alternatives together. Dissolution's grouping (relations.rkt:2901-2960) then reads 3 product worldviews. test-solver-context.rkt:326-339 pins this tagging. In the model, 177's fix shape leaves both shapes wrong (4/8 rows), and adding (b)+(c) fixes them (8/8).
findings.direction: Extend DEFERRED 177's table with these rows and its fix shape with: no network-wide tag source or viewpoint (labels come from the writing propagator, as dependent-entry assumption-id already allows); unlabelled readers lifted per entry or on the union-closure; ⊤ under ev_W ⇒ nogood(W). Land the rows in test-solver-parity.rkt (W2-6-4).
findings.falsifier: A HEAD build where these two programs give DFS's answers under :strategy atms, or a demonstration that 177's (a)+(b)+(c) alone, implemented in relations.rkt and decision-cell.rkt, passes w26-parity-ext.rkt's R5 and R6 rows.

findings.section: D.2 §6.3 row 1 read side (D2L-1); §6.5; C4-4 and C2-4's direction for (b)
findings.claim_attacked: C4-4: 'Delete the network-wide fallback read of cell-1 in net-cell-read'. D.2 row 1: 'live is read only at boundaries'.
findings.evidence: Cell-1 has a third role: the default viewpoint that makes a committed speculation visible. Commit is 'NOTHING at the network level; worldview-cache retains the hypothesis bit' (elab-speculation-bridge.rkt:305-309). meta-universe.rkt:257-263 records that without the fallback, test-speculation-bridge.rkt 'success — keeps meta-state' (:69-88) broke. w26-premise.out: (b) with no commit rule reads bot throughout and fails that test. Reading live inside S0 reproduces today's non-monotone read (bot Bool Bool top Bool): an unlabelled reader sees h2's tentative Nat as ⊤ while h2's thunk runs. A grow-only premise set P, read as W_p ∪ P, gives (bot bot Bool Bool Bool): monotone, final Bool. metavar-store.rkt:504 already reads at W = current-worldview-bitmask or 0, never cell-1, so it disagrees with meta-universe.rkt:283-300 about committed entries today.
findings.direction: Add P (committed premises) to α. Success writes P := P ∪ {h}; failure writes the nogood. Every unlabelled reader uses W_p ∪ P, which is monotone because ev_W is monotone in W for join domains. Boundary readers use live(α). An alternative is to relabel at commit (entries with labels ⊇ {h} lose h), a monotone act at the boundary.
findings.falsifier: test-speculation-bridge.rkt passes with the cell-1 fallback removed from net-cell-read, meta-universe.rkt and resolve-worldview-bitmask/pnet, and nothing else changed.

findings.section: D.2 §6.3 row 1; §6.6 (Tier 1 'stays as it is', SC-20); DEFERRED 178
findings.claim_attacked: That splitting cell-1 is local to the worldview's merge and readers.
findings.evidence: BSP picks the Tier-1 flush when `(zero? worldview)` holds (propagator.rkt:3410-3430) and every worklist propagator is fire-once with empty inputs. Every bitmask-gated goal write has exactly that shape (relations.rkt:2148, :2161, :2183). Today solver-assume makes cell-1 nonzero whenever an assumption exists, so speculative networks take Tier 2. Under (b) cell-1 is never written. w26-combined.out T1 (FULL config: pick z, x = y, then a late fire-once write x = c): under BSP, cell-1 = 0, the dependent unify fires 0 times, and y stays unbound (wrong). The control with a plain propagator fires it 2 times (right), and so does the drain.
findings.direction: Make the Tier-1 dispatch read 'no assumption exists' from α (or the assumptions cell), not from cell-1. Better, fix DEFERRED 178 so that Tier 1 drains its own writes' dependents. Sequence it before or with P1a row 1.
findings.falsifier: A production path where, once cell-1 is no longer written, a later run-to-quiescence never sees a worklist made only of fire-once empty-input propagators on a network that has dependents.
